title: Lung-protective ventilation and ventilator-induced lung injury

steps.tx: **ARDSNet** compared 6 mL/kg **predicted body weight** with 12 mL/kg, and limited **plateau pressure** to 30 cmH2O. The lower volume reduced mortality. The volume is predicted body weight, not the weight on the bed. An obese patient is harmed if you use actual weight and call it lung protection.

steps.tx: **Predicted body weight** in kilograms is 50 plus 0.91 times height in centimetres minus 152.4 for men. For women it is 45.5 plus 0.91 times height in centimetres minus 152.4. Height, not the bed weight, is what sets the tidal volume. Guessing height from a habit is how patients receive 12 mL/kg by another name.

steps.tx: **Volutrauma** is overdistension. **Barotrauma** is high transpulmonary pressure with air leak. **Atelectrauma** is repeated opening and closing of alveoli. **Biotrauma** is mediator release from those injuries. The names describe mechanisms. A patient can have more than one at the same time if the tidal volume is large and the PEEP is too low.

right.title: Too little end-expiratory volume
points: PEEP is the tool, not a bigger breath

steps.tx: The ARDSNet lower **PEEP** and FiO2 table was the table used in the original volume trial. Later trials of a higher PEEP table, including **ALVEOLI**, did not show a mortality benefit in unselected ARDS. Higher PEEP is a choice for a very hypoxaemic patient whose right ventricle can tolerate it, not a new default for every intubation.

steps.tx: The **ART trial** of a lung **recruitment** manoeuvre plus PEEP titration increased mortality. Routine recruitment manoeuvres are not used. A brief rise in pressure to open collapsed lung can drop the blood pressure at once. If you ever recruit, watch the circulation and stop when it fails. Do not make it a protocol for every new ARDS admission.

steps.tx: **Permissive hypercapnia** is accepted so that tidal volume and plateau pressure stay safe. In the ARDSNet protocol the pH was allowed to fall to 7.15, and bicarbonate was permitted below that. Chasing a normal carbon dioxide with bigger breaths recreates the injury the trial prevented. A rising carbon dioxide is tolerated. A falling pH below 7.15 is reassessed.

steps.tx: **Mechanical power** is the combination of tidal volume, pressure, flow, and respiratory rate. Higher power is associated with worse outcomes. There is no single mandated safe cutoff to write on a ventilator order. Lowering the rate, the volume, or the driving pressure is what lowers power. Do not quote a magic number the trials did not set.

right.title: What is not true
points: No single safe cutoff is mandated
Power is not a ventilator mode
Association is not a new order

steps.tx: **Driving pressure** above 15 cmH2O tracks mortality in observational ARDS data. It is plateau pressure minus PEEP. Limiting it means lowering tidal volume, or raising PEEP only when that does not push plateau pressure into an unsafe range. A lower driving pressure bought by a dangerous plateau is not a win.
